Key Approaches for Consideration
• Support political will for reform and
• Support Doing Development
reformers
Democratically
- Build relationships with
reformers and insiders alike,
enabling (and identifying)
openings
- Develop a diplomatic plan with
the CDCS and IP workplans
- Democracy Dividends for
Development and Vice Versa
- Integrated programming is
an investment (not a tax)
- Hire politically aware
staffing, not just programs

Questions for Discussion
• What approaches have you tried to support democratic
development and combat backsliding?
• What trade offs do you face supporting democratic
governance? How do we balance DRG goals with other
USG/USAID interests?
• What advice/asks do you have for Washington?

BREAKOUT GROUP INSTRUCTIONS
• Purpose: Deep dive discussions on key DRG challenges
• Choose One break out Session:
- Mitigating Mis/Dis/Malinformation,
- Combating Corruption, or
- Working in Politically Dynamic Contexts
• Product from session: Plenary shareout
• Length ofTime - 30 minutes
15

Group I: Mis/Dis/Malinformation and USAID
Questions for Discussion:
- Has MDM affected USAID in your country; what has been the
your Mission's approach to address it?
- Does your mission have an operational approach or Mission plan
to mitigate it (ie. DOCS, cybersecurity, social media analytics)?
What would that look like or require?
- How can your Mission better prepare staff and IPs for MDM?
Contact: Vera Zakem, DDI/DRG, [contact omitted]
16

Group 2: Combating Corruption
• What does this new direction mean for you, as you engage with
country counterparts, develop new strategies, programs, staffing
decisions, etc?
• What new flexibilities or other support from Washington would you
need to execute on these new directions?
• What questions are you grappling with and where would it be useful
to learn from others?
Contact: Melissa Brown,Anticorruption Task Force,
[contact omitted]
17

Group 3:Working in Politically Dynamic Contexts
• What diplomatic efforts or strategies have you used to address
democratic backsliding (or democratic openings)? What holds you back?
• What operational issues do you face in addressing these challenges and
what would help you manage them? (i.e. local political economy advisers,
cybersecurity, media analytics, crisis communications)
• Democratic openings are crucial but they can close quickly. What should
USAID do to prepare for them and keep them open?
Contact: Laura Pavlovic, DDI/DRG, [contact omitted]
